processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Solution treatment was applied to the sheets prior to cold rolling; it is the parent process (proc_solution-1100c-1h) of the 10% cold-rolling step.

Cold rolled to 10% thickness reduction (ε = 0.1) after solution treatment at 1100 °C for 1 h; grouped in the low-to-medium reduction (10%–50%) stage I producing a Taylor-lattice-type low energy dislocation structure.

structures.overall_structure: Taylor-lattice-type low energy dislocation structure (LEDS) produced by planar dislocation glide; consists of multiple slip bands. Characteristic of stage I (10%–50% rolling reduction), with gradual refinement of the slip-band spacing.

grain_structure.texture: Almost random distribution prior to cold rolling; overall rolling texture is weak

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenitic matrix

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation pile-up at the intersection of non-coplanar slip bands
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The interaction of the non-coplanar slip bands was not strong enough to completely impede dislocation glide, so dislocations could cross the intersection, making the slip bands run across the whole grain; dislocation cross slip might occur at the intersection.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar dislocation glide dominates; Taylor-lattice structure formed by multiple slip bands. Dislocation cross slip might occur at the intersections of slip bands.
interfaces.phase_evolution: No phase transformation reported for 10% reduction; austenitic matrix with κ'-carbides retained from the as-quenched state.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone-shaped tensile specimen, gauge length 16 mm, width 4 mm, cut along the rolling direction
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile test using SHIMADZU AG-X 50KN universal testing machine; three parallel tensile tests per condition

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: electrolytically polished then etched with 1 g ferric chloride + 10 ml hydrochloric acid + 10 ml deionized water; longitudinal section RD×ND
characterization_methods.purpose: observe and characterize the cold-rolled microstructure morphology of the 10% reduction sample (Fig. 3(a))
characterization_methods.key_findings: 10% reduction: equiaxed grains crossed by sets of fine, straight, parallel slip bands whose spacing differs from grain to grain, indicating inhomogeneous deformation more pronounced in favorably oriented grains.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2100 transmission electron microscope; specimens prepared by twin jet electro-polishing with 30% nitric acid + 70% methyl alcohol
characterization_methods.purpose: detailed investigation of the Taylor-lattice / slip-band substructure of the 10% rolled sample (Fig. 4(a))
characterization_methods.key_findings: The Taylor lattice consists of multiple slip bands; dislocations in the slip bands are approximately parallel and dislocation pile-ups occur at the intersections of the slip bands (green arrows, Fig. 4(a)).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku D/MAX 2500PC x-ray diffractometer; incomplete pole figures {111}, {200}, {220} measured on the RD×TD plane; ODF and f_max calculated by the Arbitrarily Defined Cells method
characterization_methods.purpose: characterize the texture evolution with cold rolling reduction (10% column of Fig. 8)
characterization_methods.key_findings: The overall texture intensity of the steel is weak; the initial texture is almost random. The α-fiber increases monotonically with rolling reduction while the Cu {112}<111> and S components increase at low-to-medium reductions before decreasing.

computational_details.simulation_method: analytical calculation of the critical shear stress for deformation twinning
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated critical stress ~1.48 GPa is much higher than the maximum resolved shear stress ~0.75 GPa, yet twinning is observed; attributed to SRO-dislocation interaction and local stress concentration.

analytical_models.model_name: critical shear stress for deformation twinning

parameters.name: b_p (Burgers vector of a partial dislocation)

analytical_models.model_note: SFE (~108 mJ/m²) and b_p (0.146 nm) are alloy-level values; the calculation concerns the twinning mechanism relevant to cold rolling of this steel.

unmapped_findings: The 10% cold-rolled sample lies in stage I (10%–50% rolling reduction) of the two-stage microstructure evolution and is characterized as a Taylor-lattice-type low energy dislocation structure (LEDS) arising from planar dislocation glide (b0023).

For the 10% rolled condition the tensile properties are only shown as the 10% curve in Fig. 1; no numeric yield strength, ultimate tensile strength or elongation values are reported in the text for this specific sample (b0020, figure_001).
The strengthening mechanism of the steel at low rolling reduction (10–30%) is the refinement of the slip-band spacing (b0065).
The stacking fault energy of the steel is ~108 mJ/m² and the Burgers vector of a partial dislocation is 0.146 nm (alloy-level values) (b0007, b0045).
